payload.title: Fact-checking and hallucination defense at every level
payload.description:
Ryan 2026-11-03: standardize fact-checking and hallucination defense at various levels, with different safeguards. Everything a model writes that a person or another agent will rely on goes through one shared check, in layers from cheap and certain to costly and judged. Live evidence: research packet 3 on Machines on Machines wrote "Rodney Reid" (source says only "Reid"; he is Randal Quran Reid) and "Tennessee resident Christopher Gatlin" (St. Louis), despite the prompt rule against adding facts. Prompt rules are not a safeguard by themselves.

LAYERS
1. Instructions to the writer: exists, necessary, not sufficient.
2. Citations exist: every claim cites a real source (exists for research and ideas).
3. Literal check (code, free, certain): each name, number, date, place and quotation in a claim must appear in the sources it cites.
4. Independent judge (separate model call, told nothing about how the text was written): does the cited text support this claim? It must give a verbatim supporting quote, and code verifies the quote. Fails closed.
5. Source strength: how many independent sources, whether a claim rests on one, and whether a party's allegation stays attributed as an allegation.
6. Consequences: a failed claim is never silently deleted and never passed on as fact. It is held in an unverified list with the reason, and later agents see it labelled.
7. People: the editor sees each claim's status; a hard gate before publishing through `review_requests`.

WHERE: research packets (first), Reference summaries, idea drafts, Story drafts before publishing, then agent conversations on Chatticus.
